title: Bihar Engineering University, Patna B.Tech. 1st Semester Examination, 2024 Engineering Mechanics Time: 03 Hours Code: 100105 Full Marks: 70
instructions: The marks are indicated in the right-hand margin.
There are NINE questions in this paper.

questions.title: Q.1 Choose the correct answer of the following (Any seven question only):

subQuestions.text: In order to determine the effects of a force acting on a body, we must know
options: Its magnitude and direction of the line along which it acts.
Its nature (whether push or pull).
Point through which it acts on the body.
All of the above.

subQuestions.text: A rigid body is in equilibrium if sum of all the
options: forces and moments acting on it is zero
moments acting on it zero
forces acting on it is zero only
couple moment acting on it is zero

subQuestions.text: Free-body diagram means
options: the diagram of a body with applied forces
the diagram drawn with free hand
the diagram of a freely suspended body
the diagram of a body with applied forces, self-weight and reactions.

subQuestions.text: The unit of power in S.I. units
options: Joule
Watt
Horsepower
kg-m

subQuestions.text: The coefficient of friction depends upon
options: Area of contact
Nature of surfaces
Shape of the surfaces
All of the above

subQuestions.text: A propped cantilever will have _____ redundant reaction.
According to Lami's theorem, the three forces
options: must be equal
must be at 120° to each other
must be both of the above
may not be any of the above

subQuestions.text: The term 'virtual work' refers to
options: actual work done by virtual forces
virtual work done by actual forces
virtual work done by virtual forces
actual work done by actual forces

subQuestions.text: Theorem of perpendicular axis is used in obtaining the moment of inertia of a
options: triangular lamina
circular lamina
square lamina
semicircular lamina (or any plane lamina)

subQuestions.text: Which of the following statements is false about trusses?
options: Bent members are never used in a truss
All members in the truss are two force members
Internal hinges are used to connect members in a truss
Wooden members can be used in trusses

subQuestions.text: A machine component 1.5 m long and weight 1000 N is supported by two ropes AB and CD as shown in Fig. 1 given below. Calculate the tensions \( T_1 and T_2 \) in the ropes AB and CD.
Show that the algebraic sum of the resolved part of a number of forces in a given direction, is equal to the resolved part of their resultant in the same direction.

State the principle of virtual work, and explain how it can be used for solving problems in statics. Two beams AE and BD are supported on rollers at B and C as shown in Figure. Determine the reactions at the rollers B and C, using the method of virtual work.
State the laws of motion. Discuss the first law in the light of second law.

A race car travels around a circular track that has a radius of 300 m. If the car increases its speed at a constant rate of \( 7 m/s^2 \) starting from rest, determine the time needed for it to reach an acceleration of \( 10 m/s^2 \).
A body consisting of a cone and a hemisphere of radius r fixed on the same base, rests on a table. Find the greatest height h of the cone, so that the combined body may stand upright.
What is a frame? Discuss its classification. Distinguish between a perfect frame and an imperfect frame.
Find the moment of inertia of a hollow sphere with respect to a diameter if the unit weight of the material is \( gamma \) and if the outer and inner radii are \( r_o \) and \( r_i \), respectively.

The coefficient of static friction between the block A and the cart B is \( mu \). If the assembly is released from rest on the inclined plane, determine the smallest value of \( mu \) that will prevent the block from sliding on the cart. Find the answer as a function of \( heta \).
State and explain D'Alembert's principle.

A uniform disc of radius r is allowed to roll down a rough inclined plane whose angle of inclination with the horizontal is \( \theta \). Prove that the linear acceleration of the disc is given by: \( a = \frac{g \sin \theta}{\frac{r^2 + k^2}{r^2}} \) where k is the radius of gyration.
